Initializer-list copy-construction of the two vectors replaces default-construction followed by copy-assignment, letting each member be built in place in a single step and avoiding the redundant empty-vector setup and assignment dispatch.

```cpp
FieldBase::FieldBase(const FieldBase &field)
    : values(field.values), stringIndexes(field.stringIndexes)
{
}
```

The function is a copy constructor. Current implementation copies `values` and `stringIndexes` members. We can't change the struct definition. We can make it faster by using initializer list instead of assignment, avoiding default construction of the members first.

Let's check what types these are. In FIT SDK, FieldBase has:

```cpp
FIT_STRING_INDEXES stringIndexes; // std::vector<FIT_UINT16>? or std::vector<FIT_UINT8>
```
Actually `FIT_MESG_VALUES` is `std::vector<FIT_MESG_VALUE>` and `FIT_STRING_INDEXES` is `std::vector<FIT_UINT16>`.

Using member initializer list: `: values(field.values), stringIndexes(field.stringIndexes)` avoids default-constructing empty vectors then assigning. That's slightly faster (avoids two allocations that get discarded). For a copy of non-empty vectors, assignment copies; initializer-list copy constructs directly. Both are one allocation. But default construction is trivial and cheap; the assignment operator of vector reuses existing capacity (which is zero for fresh default vector) so it allocates once anyway. So the gain is small.
